haiku-low.q1: A human runs the failover tool after on-call is paged. Monitoring only pages on-call when /healthz fails at 2 of 3 sites; it never fails over by itself.
haiku-low.q2: If the replica's lag over 30 s, the failover halts and unlocks. It proceeds only if rerun with the accept-data-loss override, or it is aborted.
haiku-low.q3: Before promote: flag flipped to B, write grants pulled best effort, fence sleep done, lag check passed or overridden. Before workers: promote and requeue done. Before DNS: DR scaled and green.
haiku-low.q4: Sessions are not carried over. Redis is per region and not replicated, so users log in again on the standby.
haiku-low.q5: Its state is snapshotted for inspection of lost writes, then wiped and rebuilt as a replica of the DR site from a base backup. Returning to A is a separate planned switchover.
haiku-low.q6: Read-only fencing by the witness flag. Apps and workers stop writing without a good read naming their region within 15 s, so A goes read-only within 20 s.
haiku-low.q7: The witness, a 3-node strongly consistent KV cluster across A, B and Region C. Only the runbook tool writes it, including abort. Every app box and worker in A and B reads it every 5 s.
haiku-low.q8: Jobs marked running are set back to queued in the promoted DB and rerun by DR workers after they start. Jobs must be idempotent, keyed by job id.
haiku-low.q9: Run failover --to B again; it takes the lease and resumes at the first step lacking a done line. Failover --abort returns to A only before the promote has a started line; after that it is refused.
haiku-low.q10: Requests keep landing on A until cached DNS expires, up to 60 s after cutover. If A is up they get stale reads and 503 on writes; if A is down they fail. Then they reach B.
haiku-low.q11: Commits A made that the replica never received. If A died, at most the replica's recorded lag, max 30 s unless overridden. If A was partitioned and kept writing, commits until it stopped, at most 20 s after step 2, are also lost.

sonnet.q1: A human runs the failover tool (failover --to B), after the pager fires. Monitoring (3 probe sites, GET /healthz every 10 s, 3 consecutive fails at 2 of 3 sites) only pages on-call; it never fails over by itself.
sonnet.q2: If the replica's recorded lag is over 30 s, the tool halts and releases the lease (log keeps its place). It continues only if rerun with the accept-data-loss override; otherwise the operator can abort (abort possible only before promote is started).
sonnet.q3: Before promote (step 4): lease taken (1), flag flipped to B, grant-pulling attempted on old primary, 20 s sleep done (2), and lag check ok or overridden (3), with each step's done line written. Before DR workers start (step 6): promote done (4) and requeue of running jobs done (5). Before DNS/GTM cutover (8): DR scaled (6) and green (7): standby LB and probes both pass /healthz, polled up to 5 min.
sonnet.q4: Sessions are lost: Redis is per region and not replicated, so everyone has to log in again on the standby. This is accepted.
sonnet.q5: No auto failback. The old primary's Postgres is snapshotted (to inspect lost writes), then wiped and rebuilt as a replica of the DR site from a base backup. Going back to A is a separate planned switchover later; A's app tier stays read-only meanwhile since the flag says B.
sonnet.q6: The witness-flag fence: every app box and worker polls active_region every 5 s and may start a DB write only if it had a good read in the last 15 s naming its own region (writes capped at 5 s); otherwise it goes read-only. So A is done committing 20 s after the flag names B or after it loses the witness (it can't reach a 2-of-3 quorum). Pulling write grants in step 2 is only best effort.
sonnet.q7: The witness: a 3-node strongly consistent KV cluster (one node each in A, B, Region C; reads and writes need 2 of 3) holds the active_region flag (also the lease and failover_log). Only the runbook tool (including its abort) writes it; every app box and worker in A and B reads it by polling every 5 s.
sonnet.q8: Jobs are rows in the jobs table so they replicate with the DB. In step 5, before any DR workers exist, jobs marked running in the promoted DB are set back to queued, and DR workers rerun them after step 6. Jobs A finished in its last unreplicated seconds also run again. This is fine because jobs must be idempotent (keyed by job id).
sonnet.q9: Resume: the lease expires within 30 s if the tool dies (or it stops on purpose and releases it); rerun failover --to B, which takes the lease and resumes at the first step without a done line, redoing a half-done step (all steps safe to repeat). Going back to A: only via failover --abort, and only before the promote has a started line (refused after, even if the tool died mid-promote). Abort takes the lease, sets the flag back to A, restores the app role's write grants on A's DB if they were pulled, and closes the log; A boxes resume writing on their next good poll, within 5 s.
sonnet.q10: From step 2 until their cached DNS expires (up to the 60 s TTL after GTM cutover) they still land on A. If A is up, they get reads from its stale DB and a 503 'read-only, retry shortly' on writes; if A is down, requests just fail. After the cache expires they reach B.
sonnet.q11: Whatever A committed that the replica never received (async WAL streaming). If A died: at most the replica's recorded lag, max 30 s unless the override was used. If A was partitioned and kept committing after the replica lost the stream, its commits until it stopped writing (at the latest 20 s after step 2) are also lost; the lag check can't see these, and they exist only in the old primary's snapshot.
